content: MCEF, also known as the Major Cdk9-interacting elongation factor, is a transcription factor that is closely associated with Af4. It represents the fourth member of the Af4 family (AFF) of transcription factors. This protein plays a role in various pathological conditions, including Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL), abnormal central nervous system (CNS) development, breast cancer, and azoospermia. MCEF has been shown to interact with the human-specific co-factor P-TEFb, which is essential for HIV-1 transcription. Furthermore, it has the ability to suppress HIV-1 replication. Due to these properties, MCEF (also referred to as AFF4 or AF5q31) holds potential for future therapeutic applications. The MCEF gene was originally cloned and named by Mario Clemente Estable during his tenure as a post-doctoral fellow in the laboratory of Robert G. Roeder at Rockefeller University.
